title: Automate KMS/HSM & TLS rotation for Private Installer — Helm + Terraform automation
author: Maya Singh
description: Background: Private deployments require periodic KMS/HSM key rotations and TLS certificate renewal. Historically customers performed manual steps (Vault unseal, KMS key scheduling, Helm upgrade, sealed-secrets re-encryption). This PR automates that end-to-end path for the private-installer: 1) Terraform modules to create/rotate AWS KMS keys (with optional HSM-backed keys) and corresponding IAM resources, 2) Helm chart hooks and controller changes to trigger safe in-cluster TLS cert rotation and sealed-secrets rewrap, 3) Integration with Vault (optional) for storing rotated keys and automating unseal via providers, and 4) upgrade/rollback tooling to orchestrate a safe rollout with canary+rollback on health checks. The description below is a single continuous string containing motivation, design, and rollout notes. Changes: - New terraform/modules/kms rotation module with IAM roles, key policy template, and rotation schedule support. - Optional hsm_profile flag toggles HSM-backed key creation. - Helm chart: private-installer/templates/cert-rotation-job.yaml implements an idempotent post-upgrade Job that obtains new certs from the configured PKI (self-hosted CA or Vault cert engine), caches them to sealed-secrets, and performs a rolling restart of control-plane pods with health probes. - Controller: a small rotation-controller (k8s job) added to detect missing / nearing-expiry certs and trigger rotation flow with a leader-election guard. - Sealed-secrets: added rewrap helper that uses the cluster KMS/HSM to re-encrypt static secrets after key rotation. - Vault: optional vault-integration path (docs and scripts) to store master unseal tokens and rotated keys; added helm values to enable. - Upgrade tooling: installer/upgrade.sh obtains rotation plan from Terraform outputs and runs a dry-run rotation then a canary target, with automatic rollback on probe failures. - e2e/integration: new CI job in the private-installer pipeline that runs terraform apply using a mock provider, runs helm upgrade to exercise post-upgrade jobs, and asserts secret continuity and TLS validity. Checklist (included in PR body): - [x] Terraform module implemented and unit tested. - [x] Helm hooks implemented and tested locally. - [x] Sealed-secrets rewrap helper implemented and integration tested. - [x] Vault optional integration documented. - [x] Upgrade/rollback script added and manual runbook updated. - [x] e2e CI job added to private-installer pipeline. Backwards compatibility: default install path unchanged. All automation is opt-in via values.yaml and terraform variable flags to avoid surprising existing customers. Rollout plan: merge to main behind feature flag and ship as minor release. Enable for a small set of early-access customers for two weeks, collect metrics (rotation success, latency, failed rollbacks), then gradually enable by default. Risks & mitigations: - KMS/HSM misconfiguration can prevent sealed-secrets decryption: mitigation includes dry-run mode and a safe rollback path that restores previous key and secrets snapshots. - Vault unavailability: fallback to manual unseal and operator runbook. - Post-rotation downtime: rotation is performed with rolling restarts and health probe checks; automated rollback triggers if >5% of pods fail Liveness checks during canary. Documentation & runbooks updated in docs/private-installer/rotation.md.
